chunks: Ali ibn Mahziyar from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about recitation behind the Imam in the last two rak'ahs, so he said: 'The Imam recites the Opening of the Book, and those behind him glorify (God). If you are alone, then recite in them, and if you wish, then glorify (God).'
ai.seo_question: What should a follower do with their recitation during the last two rak'ahs of prayer behind an Imam?
ai.summary: Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar reports from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) that in the last two rak'ahs of prayer, the Imam recites Al-Fatiha while followers may choose to recite it themselves or remain silent in glorification (tasbih). This hadith highlights the flexibility (rukhsah) in Shia jurisprudence regarding recitation behind the Imam, contrasting with stricter views that prohibit it entirely, and establishes that recitation is obligatory only when praying individually (munfarid).
